nodes.question: What does the MMI stand for, and what does it amalgamate?
nodes.answer: MMI stands for Multi-Metric Index, and it is an amalgamation of several community-related indices that differ between river types, designed to reflect the impact of various stressors on water bodies.

The MMI is an amalgamation of several community-related indices (dif - fering between river types), which was designed to reflect the impact of various stressors including alterations of morphology, hydrology and water quality (Hering et al. 2006). The German Fauna Index serves as the core com - ponent of the MMI, assessing the presence of river-type specific indicator species, while additional metrics, such as the proportion of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (%EPT), the share of rheophilic species, and the number of Trichoptera species, provide further eco - logical context. We here used the standardized version of the MMI ranging between 0 (worst) to 1 (best), the main basis for the ecological status calculation under the WFD (European Commission 2000). For simplification reasons, we refer to the MMI as the ecological status in the fol - lowing. A comparison of the MMI with other commonly used biodiversity indices (Shannon diversity, Evenness, and Richness) is provided in Supplementary Figure S2.
